content.comment_body: Hello, I'm using [version_no]. Adjusting input and output signal numbers is straightforward, but I'm not able to change block numbers. It would make navigation easier if blocks could be re-ordered on the unit, rather than having to sequence them from the start. Is there a fix for this?
I'm not entirely sure about your request, but have you tried changing the block name instead?

[user_name] wants to modify block numbers, but these are assigned automatically. Each new block gets an incremented number, so if you add blocks to an existing program, the sequence may seem illogical when viewing the display. As far as I know, block numbers can't be changed. If this is an issue, you could print out your diagram and include it in your electrical documentation. If you have [product_name] software, why not edit the program there instead of directly on the device?

I've written several programs and didn't realize that block sequence couldn't be adjusted afterwards. Customers often request organized block arrangements, but now I know this can't be changed once set.

Hi [user_name], I’ve shared information in the German section about motivations for sorting block numbers and the procedure for doing so: "Notes on sorting blocks whose parameters can be edited in RUN mode." The main reasons are easier direct programming on [product_name] modules, improved documentation, and more effective use of parameter assignment mode during program execution. Parameter changes are possible as long as default protection mode remains active. However, blocks in this mode are sorted only by their numbers (not names or types), which can hinder efficient parameter editing, especially for function groups. [user_name] is correct: block numbers cannot be changed via program functions, only manually. Here are some methods, but planning is necessary: 0) You only need sorted block numbers for parameter editing; blocks with protection mode disabled are ignored. 1) If you have spare blocks, insert dummy blocks to push numbering up, then create the sequence you want. 2) If no spare blocks are available, carefully use free numbers within the range, filling gaps with dummy blocks if needed, then rebuilding your program. 3) For larger changes, start a new program, planning the block arrangement with dummy blocks and then transferring necessary blocks across, reconnecting and setting parameters as needed. Regards, [user_name]. Useful links: Collection of notes and circuits for [product_name], Signal scaling, Retrieving data, Math equations with [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users face limitations with automatically generated block numbers in the programming environment, making navigation and parameter management more difficult on the device and during documentation for clients. Manual workarounds are available but are time-consuming and add complexity, as assigning block numbers directly is not supported.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are seeking the option to freely assign or reorganize block numbers in the programming software for improved workflow and documentation.
